args.text:
Batch: 25 runs. 6 accepted, 6 declined, 13 not reported.
Flagged (5), reason width_free_ratio_used: r05, r13, r16, r19, r24. Each passes rigid-body invariance and closure, and the median REGR peak, peak position and growth-zone length are typical of the batch (all |z| < 1). But each run's only kept remedy was switching to the width-free ratio. That switch skipped the plane-sections check, whose values (3.43–3.86 %/h) are above the 3.25 threshold.
Cleared (1): r17. It passes rigid-body invariance and closure, its skipped plane-sections value is 0.571 %/h, and every summary is close to the batch (largest |z| = 1.38).
What the flagged runs have in common: the width-free ratio was used in place of fixing a curvature-rate mismatch. Their flank strain-rate differences group at about -3.5 to -3.9 %/h, and their width-free ratios group at about -0.42 to -0.47. Neither matches the width-free runs whose plane-sections values pass (0.57–1.34 %/h).
